title: Enquiries Made In Respect Of G.W. Spence, Ex-Member Of The Smp

page_data.en:

G. 40M-9-35

L.C.C.

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
File No. ____
Date S. 2. XXXXXX
REPORT
Date. December 13, 19 35.

Subject G.W. Spence.

Made by D.P.S. Henchman Forwarded by [签名]

Enquiries made in respect of G.W. Spence,
ex-member of the S.M.P., disclose that following the
termination of his services with the Police on Sept. 28,
1933 he was engaged in wireless repair work of a private
nature until June 20, 1934 when he obtained employment with
the shipping firm of Moller Bros., 30 Foochow Road.
With this firm, in the capacity of junior accountant,
he remained until June 30, 1935 when he resigned, telling
his employers that he had received an invitation from the
local Soviet Embassy to proceed to Vladivostock and from
thence to Siberia where he was to obtain employment as a
lumber expert. Spence does not appear to have availed
himself of this invitation, for he remained, unemployed,
in Shanghai until August when he applied to the
secretary of the Anzac Society for repatriation to
Australia, his native country. His application
was successful and he was granted a passage on s.s.
"Tanda", in which vessel, occupying Cabin No.68, Spence
left Shanghai on August 9.
Enquiries made at Mackinnon and Mackenzie's,
agents for the above vessel, show that s.s. "Tanda" sailed
from Shanghai to Japan, where she visited Nagasaki, Kobe
and Yokohama, leaving the latter port on August 25, arriving
in Hongkong on August 31 and in Sydney on September 20.
It is impossible that the Major Spence, whom
Rosa York stated she met in Hongkong, could be identical
with G.W. Spence, for Rosa York arrived in Hongkong on
July 31 and G.W. Spence was in Shanghai on that date.
Having sailed, ostensibly with the intention

上海公共租界工部局警务处。
档案号 ____
日期 S. 2. XXXXXX
报告
日期：1935年12月13日。

事由：G.W. Spence。

由 D.P.S. Henchman 制作 转呈 [签名]

经对前上海公共租界工部局警务处（S.M.P.）成员 G.W. Spence 进行调查，查明其在1933年9月28日结束警队服役后，从事私人性质的无线电修理工作，直至1934年6月20日受雇于福州路30号的马勒兄弟公司（Moller Bros.）。他在该公司担任初级会计师，直至1935年6月30日辞职，并告知雇主他已收到当地苏联大使馆的邀请，将前往符拉迪沃斯托克（Vladivostock），随后前往西伯利亚，在那里担任木材专家。Spence 似乎并未接受此邀请，因为他一直失业留在上海，直到8月份向澳新协会（Anzac Society）秘书申请遣返回其祖国澳大利亚。他的申请获得批准，并获准乘坐“坦达”号轮船（s.s. "Tanda"）启程，Spence 占据68号舱位，于8月9日离开上海。
经向上述船只的代理行麦金农与麦肯齐公司（Mackinnon and Mackenzie's）查询，显示“坦达”号从上海驶往日本，停靠长崎、神户和横滨，于8月25日离开横滨港，8月31日抵达香港，9月20日抵达悉尼。
Rosa York 称她在香港遇到的 Major Spence 不可能是 G.W. Spence，因为 Rosa York 于7月31日抵达香港，而 G.W. Spence 当日身在上海。既然已经启航，表面上是打算

one might suppose that Spence is now resident in Australia,
possibly at his father's address, Cameron Street, Wauchope,

There is, however, a possibility that
Spence either did not reach his home or that he broke
his journey in Japan. This possibility arises from
the fact that it is reported that Spence was seen between
September 21 and 26 in Tokyo by a Mr. Witte, former
employee of Moller Bros. in Shanghai and now employed
by Massey & Co. of Yokohama.
The above mentioned shipping agents have
no record of the journey having been broken but they
state that had Spence wished to do so nothing in their
regulations could have prevented him.

前往澳大利亚，且持有不可转让的船票，人们可能会认为 Spence 现在居住在澳大利亚，可能在其父亲位于新南威尔士州沃科普（Wauchope, N.S.W.）卡梅伦街（Cameron Street）的地址。
然而，存在一种可能性，即 Spence 要么未抵达家乡，要么在日本中断了行程。这种可能性源于有报告称，前上海马勒兄弟公司员工、现任职于横滨 Massey & Co. 的 Witte 先生，在9月21日至26日期间曾在东京见过 Spence。
上述航运代理行没有中断行程的记录，但他们表示，如果 Spence 希望这样做，他们的规定中没有任何条款可以阻止他。

U.B.K. Consulate General,
Shanghai.

29. 11. 35.

My dear Givens,

Early in July we received a report from you
(verbally I think through one of the Detectives of the Special
Branch) concerning a certain G. W. SPENCE who was formerly
employed by Moller Bros. in a clerical capacity and who had
received an invitation from the local Soviet Embassy to
proceed to U.S.S.R. as a lumber expert. He is the holder
of Australian passport No. 122049 of 12.12.34.

* See L.7007
You will also remember that ROSE YORK while she
was here stated in conversation that she knew a certain Major
Spence in Hongkong but we were never able to trace this man.

It appears to us now to be barely possible that
these two are identical. Can you by any chance let us know
where G.W. Spence is at the moment.

Yours Sincerely,
〔签名〕

T.P. Givens Esq.,
Special Branch,
S.M.P.

S2,
For attention please.
JAS
29 NOV. 1935

D.S. Henchman
JAR 30/11

荷兰驻上海总领事馆，
上海。

1935年11月29日。

亲爱的 Givens，

七月初，我们收到了你的一份报告（我想是通过特科的一名侦探口头传达的），关于某位 G. W. SPENCE，他此前在马勒兄弟公司（Moller Bros.）担任文员，并收到当地苏联大使馆的邀请，以木材专家身份前往苏联。他持有1934年12月12日签发的澳大利亚护照，号码为122049。

* 见 L.7007
你也应该记得，ROSE YORK 在此地时曾在谈话中表示她认识香港的某位 Major Spence，但我们始终未能追踪到此人。

现在看来，这两人是同一人的可能性微乎其微。你能否设法告知我们 G.W. Spence 目前的下落。

此致，
敬礼，
〔签名〕

T.P. Givens 先生，
特科，
上海公共租界工部局警务处。

S2，
请予关注。
JAS
1935年11月29日

D.S. Henchman
JAR 30/11

REPORT
Date December 9, 1935.

Subject Communication from the Netherlands Consulate-General, dated
November 30, 1935, re Michael V. Masslow, Russian.

Made by D.S. Makaroff Forwarded by **〔此处转录不清〕**

Michael Vladimirovitch Masslow, Russian, was born
December 25, 1896 at Moscow.
He studied in one of the schools there and upon
graduation attended the Imperial Technical Institute on
Chemical-Engineering faculty.
However, owing to outbreak of Great War, he
discontinued his studies and entered the Kazan Military
School, where, upon passing a short course, he graduated
with the rank of first lieutenant.
In August 1915 he left for Austrian front
with the 125th Fusilier Regiment and fought in the ranks
up to 1918, when the revolution broke out. During his
actual service he received the Order of St. Anna, 3rd and
4th degree, the Order of St. Stanislav of 3rd degree and
also the Soldier's Cross of St. George, all for bravery
and highly distinguished service.
In 1918 he left the Austrian front and pro-
ceeded to the Volga Region, where he joined the White forces
of General Kappel and fought against the Bolsheviks up
to the latter part of 1918, when he was wounded at Railway
Station Cheshmy and conveyed to the Oms Military Hospital
and later transferred to Vladivostock Military Hospital,
where he was discharged in 1919.
In February 1919 he came to Shanghai and
soon afterwards secured employment with the Liulin Estate
at Kuling as custodian, in which capacity he worked up
to the end of 1919.
In 1920 he left for the Philippine Islands,
where he worked as chemist with the New Life Bazaar, Import

日期：1935年12月9日。

事由：荷兰总领事馆1935年11月30日来函，关于俄国人 Michael V. Masslow。

由 D.S. Makaroff 制作 转呈 **〔此处转录不清〕**

Michael Vladimirovitch Masslow，俄国人，1896年12月25日出生于莫斯科。
他在当地一所学校就读，毕业后进入帝国理工学院化学工程系学习。
然而，由于第一次世界大战爆发，他中断学业，进入喀山军事学校，在完成短期课程后，以少尉军衔毕业。
1915年8月，他随第125步兵团前往奥地利前线，在军中服役至1918年革命爆发。在实际服役期间，他因英勇和杰出表现，荣获三级和四级圣安娜勋章、三级圣斯坦尼斯拉夫勋章以及圣乔治士兵十字勋章。
1918年，他离开奥地利前线，前往伏尔加地区，加入卡佩尔将军（General Kappel）的白军部队，与布尔什维克作战，直至1918年下半年，他在切斯米火车站（Railway Station Cheshmy）受伤，被送往鄂木斯克（Oms）军医院，后转至符拉迪沃斯托克军医院，并于1919年退役。
1919年2月，他来到上海，不久后在牯岭（Kuling）的柳林地产（Liulin Estate）谋得看守一职，在此职位上工作至1919年底。
1920年，他前往菲律宾群岛，在新生活集市进口公司（New Life Bazaar, Import

Company, up to 1921 when he resigned from his position and
proceeded to Harbin. For the next two years he worked with
the "Riva" Printing and Publishing Co. as manager of a
printing department and also with the "Russian Daily News,"
a Russian newspaper published in English.

In May 1923 he came to Shanghai and in company with a
Mr. Cooper established the Cooper & Co., Distillery and
Perfumery Works, 301 Avenue Joffre.

This establishment closed down in 1924 owing to poor
business and Masslow proceeded to the Philippine Islands,
where at Manapla, Negros, he joined the Sugar Refinery Factory
as a chemist.

In 1929 he returned to Shanghai and established the
"St. Georges" Pharmacy at No.1559 Bubbling Well Road. He
conducted this business up to 1933 when he sold out
and left for Tsingtao.

Whilst in Tsingtao he became a shareholder and manager
of the "Tsingtao United Industrial & Trading Co.", a store
containing a stock of medical supplies.

Masslow's wife and daughter reside in Tsingtao at present.

It should be noted that Michael V. Masslow is not iden-
tical with one Moses Grigorievitch Masloff, Soviet citizen of
Jewish origin and former employee of the Centrosojus, who is
mentioned in the attached communication from the Netherlands
Consulate-General.

Nothing detrimental is known by this office against
this individual either politically or criminally.

N. McEwan
D. S.
Deputy Commissioner, Special Branch.

Company）担任化学师，直至1921年辞职前往哈尔滨。在接下来的两年里，他在“里瓦”印刷出版公司（"Riva" Printing and Publishing Co.）担任印刷部经理，并在英文出版的俄文报纸《俄罗斯日报》（"Russian Daily News"）工作。

1923年5月，他来到上海，并与一位 Cooper 先生共同创立了位于霞飞路301号的 Cooper & Co. 蒸馏与香水厂。

该机构因生意不佳于1924年关闭，Masslow 再次前往菲律宾群岛，在内格罗斯岛（Negros）的马纳普拉（Manapla）加入糖精炼厂担任化学师。

1929年，他回到上海，在静安寺路1559号创办了“圣乔治”药房（"St. Georges" Pharmacy）。他经营此项业务直至1933年，随后卖出产业前往青岛。

在青岛期间，他成为“青岛联合工贸公司”（"Tsingtao United Industrial & Trading Co."）的股东兼经理，这是一家储备医疗用品的商店。

Masslow 的妻子和女儿目前居住在青岛。

需要注意的是，Michael V. Masslow 并非 Moses Grigorievitch Masloff，后者是苏联公民，犹太裔，前中央消费合作总社（Centrosojus）员工，这在附上的荷兰总领事馆来函中有所提及。

本处室未发现此人在政治或刑事方面有任何不利记录。

N. McEwan
D. S.
副总监，特科。

November 30, 1935, re Michael V. Masslow, Russian. 

Michael Viladimirovitch Masslow, Russian, was born 
on December 25, 1896 at Moscow. — 

He studied in one of the schools there and upon 
graduation attended the Imperial Technical Institute of 
Chemical-Engineering. 

However, owing to outbreak of the Great War, he 
discontinued his studies and entered the Kazan Military 
School, where, upon passing a short course, he graduated as 
a first lieutenant. 

In August 1915 he left for the Austrian Front with 
the 125th Fusilier Regiment where he fought until 1918, when 
the revolution broke out. During his actual service he 
received the Order of St. Anma, Srd and 4th degree, the Order 
eof St. Stanislav, Srd degree, and also the Soldier's Cress of 
St. George, all for bravery and highly distinguished service. 

In 1018 he left the Austrian Front and preceeded 
to the Voaga Regien, where he joined the white forces of
